# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 12 (Bu-Vb Pc12)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc12  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 12  
**Title (English, from literature):** Speaking evasively  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aññavādaka-sikkhāpada* ("Speaking evasively", Vin IV 35–37) is the twelfth rule in the *Pācittiya* chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [Piya Tan 2002]. The rule stipulates that a monk incurs an offense requiring expiation (*pācittiya*) if he speaks evasively or causes vexation when being formally questioned during legal proceedings of the Sangha. The origin story (*nidāna*) features the obstinate monk Channa (Sanskrit Chandaka), formerly Prince Siddhārtha's charioteer, who habitually resisted instruction and counter-questioned his examiners when formal disciplinary proceedings were brought against him [Piya Tan 2002; Piya Tan 2004; Thanissaro, Samyutta Nikaya]. An English translation of the rule and its Vibhaṅga has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Equivalent *pācittiya* rules exist in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅgas and Prātimokṣa sūtras of the Sarvāstivāda (Pc 13), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 13), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 12), Mahāsāṅghika (Pc 12 or 13), and Dharmaguptaka (Pc 12) lineages, as well as in the Kāśyapīya, Upāliparipṛcchā, and parallel Bhikkhunī codes (including Theravāda Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 108).
